notes: Populated only where a published value exists for a front-foot off-side drive. Entries with band_derivation 'todo' are structurally valid but unscored - DO NOT fill them with plausible-looking numbers. A fabricated reference range produces feedback indistinguishable from correct feedback, which is the failure mode this whole design exists to prevent. Style descriptors (backlift direction, trigger movement, stance width) are deliberately absent: they are classified by style_markers.py and reported neutrally, never scored against a range. See docs/ACCURACY.md section 6.

batting.interval_se_imp.derivation: The source reports a point estimate only - front foot planted approximately 0.06 s prior to impact for the cover drive - with no dispersion. The band was widened around that point to roughly +/- one frame-detection error at the 120 fps floor plus allowance for genuine between-player variation. The width is an ASSUMPTION, not a published range. Replace with mean +/- 1 SD as soon as a source reporting dispersion is available.
batting.interval_se_imp.notes: Confidence is low because the band width is assumed rather than measured. The point estimate itself is well founded.

batting.stride_length_norm.derivation: Source reports cover-drive front-foot stride of approximately 0.68 m in absolute units. Converted to a fraction of stature using an assumed elite male cricketer stature of 1.80 m, giving 0.378. TWO assumptions are stacked here: the population mean stature, and the band width around the point estimate. Both are unverified.
batting.stride_length_norm.notes: Banded, never 'longer is better'. sarpeshkar2011 reports that experienced batters deliberately take a SHORT-to-medium stride so they can play the ball later, and pullshot_malaysia found no significant stride-length difference across skill levels. A stride above this band is not automatically a fault.

batting.lead_knee_angle_imp.notes: No cover-drive-specific published range located. pullshot_malaysia gives lower-limb angles for the PULL shot only and must not be transferred across shot types. This metric is measurable and would be Tier A - it only needs a source.

batting.lead_knee_extension_se_imp.notes: Variable is defined by peploe2019technique (lead knee extension, SE to IMP) but that study reports it as a regression input for a range-hitting task, not as a normative range for a cover drive.

batting.head_vertical_displacement_ds_im.notes: mann2013head establishes head-ball coupling as the strongest measurable batting skill discriminator (elite 2.4 +/- 1.7 deg vs club 3.7 +/- 1.4 deg mean head-ball angle), but that measure requires ball tracking. The head-lift proxy used here has no published normative band. Highest-value gap in this template - worth sourcing first.

batting.head_horizontal_displacement_ds_.notes: headcom2007 shows skilled batters hold the head further forward of the centre base point, but reports positions relative to a lab reference frame that does not transfer to a normalised video measure.

batting.stride_duration_ss_se.notes: pullshot_malaysia reports ~0.22-0.24 s stride duration for the PULL shot. Not transferable to a front-foot drive.

batting.tempo_bc_ds.notes: peploe2019technique defines BC and DS as events but reports no normative interval between them.

batting.trigger_timing.notes: Trigger PRESENCE is a descriptor and never scored (trigger_formats: prevalence varies by format, Test 56.1% to IPL 76%). Trigger TIMING relative to release could be scored if a source existed, but none was located.

batting.base_length_pct_stature_imp.notes: peploe2019technique defines 'base length (% height) IMP' as a variable and it is already scale-invariant, which makes it an ideal candidate - but the published values are for a range-hitting task, not a cover drive.

batting.com_anterior_displacement_min_im.notes: headcom2007 reports skilled batters' COM further forward at predicted contact, qualitatively.

batting.head_over_lead_knee_imp.notes: Widely coached, but no quantitative normative band located. Tier B because it is sensitive to camera obliquity.

batting.x_factor_ds.notes: peploe2019technique found X-factor at downswing start to be the single strongest predictor of bat speed (28.0% of variance), but it is a transverse-plane measure - abraham2025opencap shoulder axial rotation RMSE 28.54 deg - so it is suppressed entirely without the optional front-on camera, and Tier B even with it.
